deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page is headed 'Entfernung' (distance). It works with points in the plane by computing with them as vectors, in the style of barycentric or point arithmetic. Capital letters A–E are the vertices of a pentagon, sketched top centre with some diagonals and the sides BC and ED produced. Lower-case b, c, d, e are a second set of points (or, perhaps, their distances from a fixed line; this is my reading of the heading). Every relation written has coefficients summing to the same value on both sides, i.e. it is an affine relation. Such a relation holds both for position vectors and for signed distances from any line.

(1) Upper right: Menelaus-type sketch. Triangle ABC is cut by a transversal. The line meets BC at a point labelled +α, AB produced at a point labelled −γ, and AC at a point marked ε. The note 'Geht durch die Punkte' (passes through the points) lists αC−(1−α)B = (α−1)B+αC on BC, then εA, (γ−1)A and γB. One further entry, apparently (1−α)C, is struck out. This parametrises the intersection points of a transversal with the sides. Note that the coefficient sums here (2α−1) are not 1, so these are weighted or homogeneous points, or simply rough notes.

(2) Main computation. Parameters p, q, r, s.
(i) (ps−qr)A = p(q+s)c − q(p+r)b. Coefficient sums agree: pq+ps−pq−qr = ps−qr. So A lies on the line bc.
(ii) (q+s−ps+qr)A + (q+s−ps+qr)qC = (1+q)(q+s−ps+qr)d. Divided by the common factor this is A+qC = (1+q)d, i.e. d lies on AC dividing it in ratio q:1. Gauss pre-multiplied by K = q+s−ps+qr to prepare the elimination.
(iii) (q+qr−qs)A + KqC = q(1+q+r−ps+qr)e. Sums agree. Divided by q: (1+r−s)A + KC = (1+q+r−ps+qr)e.
(iv) (ii) minus (iii) eliminates C: [K − (q+qr−qs)]A = s(1−p+q)A = (1+q)Kd − q(1+q+r−ps+qr)e.
(v) Elimination of A: take s(1−p+q)·(i) minus (ps−qr)·(iv). This gives 0 = ps(q+s)(1−p+q)c − qs(p+r)(1−p+q)b − (ps−qr)(1+q)Kd + (ps−qr)q(1+q+r−ps+qr)e. This is an affine dependence among the four points b, c, d, e. Check (mine): the coefficients sum to (ps−qr)s(1−p+q) + (ps−qr)(−s(1−p+q)) = 0.

(3) 'Correspondirende' (the corresponding relation): 0 = sC − rB − D + (1+r−s)E. This is the affine relation among the corresponding capital points B, C, D, E; its coefficients sum to 0. The lower-case coefficients equal the capital ones times point-dependent weights. This is consistent with b, c, d, e being images of B, C, D, E under a correspondence that rescales the weights, such as a central projection. That interpretation is mine and uncertain.

The next folio repeats the same computation with p and q partly interchanged; it is probably a variant or recopy.
errors: No algebraic errors found: (i), (ii), (iii) are each balanced; (iv) follows exactly from (ii)−(iii); (v) follows exactly from s(1−p+q)(i) − (ps−qr)(iv), and its coefficients sum to zero.
In the Menelaus notes the expressions αC−(1−α)B and (γ−1)A, γB do not have coefficient sum 1. They are either weighted/homogeneous points or loose notes; the struck-out entry is abandoned.
The meaning of the lower-case letters (points vs. distances 'Entfernung') is not stated on the page, so the geometric purpose is inferred.

results.what: Representing points as affine combinations and eliminating an auxiliary point to get a linear (affine) dependence among four points
results.modern_name: Barycentric/affine coordinates; affine dependence of four coplanar points
results.usually_credited_to: A. F. Möbius, Der barycentrische Calcul (1827)

results.what: Parametrising the intersection points of a transversal with the sides of a triangle
Comparison of the affine relation among b,c,d,e with the 'corresponding' relation among B,C,D,E (coefficients rescaled by weights)
results.modern_name: Behaviour of affine relations under projective/central correspondence (weights in homogeneous coordinates)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine elimination with point arithmetic in the plane, related to Gauss's known pentagon studies of around 1823. The barycentric style is notable but was in use in his era, and nothing here goes beyond elementary affine algebra.

checkable.asserts: Equation (i) has balanced coefficient sums, so A is an affine combination of b and c.
Subtracting (iii) from (ii) gives coefficient s(1-p+q) for A, as written in (iv).
The d,e coefficient sum in (iv) equals s(1-p+q) (key step in the zero-sum check).
The final relation among c, b, d, e is an affine dependence: its coefficients sum to zero.
The 'corresponding' relation 0 = sC - rB - D + (1+r-s)E has zero coefficient sum.
The final relation is exactly s(1-p+q)*(i) minus (ps-qr)*(iv), i.e. the elimination of A.

transcription_corrections: The third line of the 'Geht durch die Punkte' list is struck out in the manuscript (apparently '(1-α)C' or similar); it is not a valid entry.
'εA' is written as a separate label (the point ε on AC in the sketch), placed above '(γ-1)A'.
The top-right folio number reads '2' (circled), with a crossed-out number followed by '3'.
In line (iii) the first coefficient is '(q + qr - qs)' with a gap after q; it is not '(q+s+qr-qs)'.
The diagram labels: pentagon A, B, C, D, E with arrows along BC, CD, DE; triangle sketch with labels B, A, C, ε, +α, -γ.
